title: 0209-vits-for-action-classification-in-videos
universal_lens: The primitive unifies spatiotemporal action classification under extreme class imbalance via a focal loss operator. It maps transient biomechanical cues into a high-dimensional token space, applying a non-linear focusing mechanism to suppress trivial negatives and isolate rare, safety-critical event manifolds.
gsi_mapping: GSI translates the focal loss output into a conformal prediction interval for tackle risk. By treating the minority-class augmentation as a Bayesian prior adjustment, GSI computes calibrated posterior probabilities of spearing mechanics, ensuring robust uncertainty quantification across varied practice environments.
gse_mapping: GSE embeds this ViViT classifier as a state-transition trigger within the situational reasoning engine. When the focal-weighted probability exceeds a dynamic threshold at the first point of contact, GSE transitions the game state to 'high-risk collision,' initiating coach-centered triage protocols.

primitives.name: Focal Loss Rare-Event Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Objective: focal loss L_FL = -α_y(1-p_y)^γ log(p_y), γ = 1.6, α_risky = 0.6 / α_safe = 0.4 — moderate focusing (90%-confident example gets 0.04 weight, 25× reduction; 50%-confident gets 0.33, 3× reduction).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: L_FL: dimensionless scalar loss; \alpha_y: dimensionless class balance factor (0.6 risky, 0.4 safe); p_y: dimensionless predicted probability; \gamma: dimensionless focusing parameter (1.6).
primitives.assumptions: Assumes independent and identically distributed video clips localized around the first point of contact. Assumes standard cross-entropy baseline is overwhelmed by safe-tackle majority class (~65/35 split).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if p_y approaches 1.0 for misclassified risky events, causing gradient vanishing. Also fails if temporal localization is poor, diluting the signal-to-noise ratio in the input frames.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to GSE's penalty-detection module. The focal weighting directly maps to the confidence score required to flag a targeting violation or injury-risk content lane event.
layer2.telemetry: Macro-F1 score on held-out validation folds; recall specifically for the risky class.

primitives.name: Spatiotemporal Tubelet Tokenizer
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Input: 32-frame clip (15 frames before + 16 after manually marked FPOC), 224×224 → (32/2)×(224/16)×(224/16) = 3,136 spatiotemporal tokens + class token.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: N_tokens: integer count (3,136); T: sequence length in frames (32); \tau: tubelet temporal stride (2); H, W: spatial dimensions in pixels (224); P: patch size in pixels (16).
primitives.assumptions: Assumes rigid spatiotemporal grid extraction preserves critical kinematic features of the tackle. Relies heavily on accurate manual marking of the First Point of Contact (FPOC).
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singularity occurs when camera motion induces severe parallax or occlusion, breaking the local stationarity assumption of the 16x16 patches. Fails entirely if FPOC is misaligned by >2 frames.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's raw video ingestion layer. This tokenization forms the foundational feature vector upon which downstream biomechanical classifiers operate.
layer2.telemetry: Embedding stability metrics; cosine similarity of extracted tokens across augmented vs. unaugmented clips.

primitives.name: Stratified Post-Split Augmentation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Augmentation applied only after stratified 5-fold split (StratifiedKFold, shuffle, seed 42), only to training folds, targeting the minority risky class to reach ~50:50 (per fold ~171–173 augmented risky clips; training 758–760 clips; validation untouched at 146–147 videos, 34.9–35.6% risky).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: Fold index: integer (1..5); N_risky_train: integer count (~171-173); N_total_train: integer count (758-760); N_val: integer count (146-147).
primitives.assumptions: Assumes data leakage is strictly prevented by applying augmentations exclusively post-split. Assumes the augmented synthetic distribution accurately reflects the underlying manifold of risky tackles.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breaks down if augmentation artifacts (e.g., unnatural lighting shifts or geometric distortions) create spurious correlations that the ViT exploits, leading to catastrophic failure on clean validation data.

layer2.mapping: Directly maps to GSI's conformal inference calibration step, where synthetic edge cases are injected to stress-test the prediction intervals of the risk model.
layer2.telemetry: Class balance ratio in training vs. validation sets; generalization gap measured by delta in macro-F1.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core mathematical structure relies on mapping a highly imbalanced spatiotemporal distribution into a discriminative latent space using Vision Transformers (ViViT). The primary challenge is the rarity of the 'risky' class (spearing mechanics), constituting roughly 35% of the dataset. Standard cross-entropy would be dominated by the majority 'safe' class gradients. The authors introduce a focal loss operator, $L_{FL} = -\alpha_y(1-p_y)^\gamma \log(p_y)$, with $\gamma=1.6$ and asymmetric $\alpha$. This acts as a non-linear filter, exponentially suppressing the loss contribution of well-classified easy examples (safe tackles), thereby forcing the optimization trajectory to focus on the hard, borderline risky instances. To further stabilize this rare-event learning, they employ a strict post-split augmentation strategy. By applying Taguchi-L18-guided augmentations *only* to the training folds after a stratified 5-fold split, they synthetically expand the minority class to a 50:50 ratio without contaminating the validation set. The input itself is a carefully constructed 32-frame window centered on a manually annotated First Point of Contact (FPOC), tokenized into 3,136 spatiotemporal patches. The duality here lies between the physical reality of a transient, high-speed collision and its discrete, tokenized representation. The failure mode emerges from the reliance on manual FPOC; if the temporal centering is off, the critical kinematic cues fall outside the receptive field of the tubelets, rendering the focal loss ineffective as it optimizes on noise. Furthermore, the modest recall (0.67) indicates that the decision boundary in the latent space still leaves a significant volume of the risky manifold unclassified, likely due to the limited diversity of dummy-tackle scenarios compared to live game collisions.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This approach inherits from Lin et al.'s (2017) introduction of Focal Loss for dense object detection, adapting it to the temporal domain of video classification. The use of ViViT (Touvron et al., 2021) represents the shift from CNN-based I3D models to pure attention mechanisms for spatiotemporal modeling. The specific application to sports biomechanics echoes earlier work by Nafi et al. (2022) on tackling datasets, but elevates it by addressing class imbalance through modern regularization techniques rather than simple oversampling.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From the perspective of the coaching staff (the decision actors), this system is not an autonomous referee but a triage assistant. They operate under high cognitive load during practice. The model's output must align with their mental model of 'dangerous form.' If the AI flags a tackle as risky based on subtle head angles that a human eye misses, the coach must trust the probabilistic assertion. The focal loss essentially mimics the coach's heightened attention to borderline cases, mathematically formalizing their expert intuition that 'almost-safe' tackles are the most critical to review.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: A strict veto condition applies if the system is deployed on raw, untrimmed game footage without an automated FPOC localization module. The current primitives assume precise temporal alignment; feeding arbitrary video segments will cause the tokenization to capture irrelevant pre- or post-contact dynamics, collapsing the macro-F1. Additionally, if the recall for the risky class drops below 0.55 in cross-validation, the primitive must be rejected for production safety lanes, as missing one in three dangerous tackles violates the fundamental utility of a risk-detection system.
